name: Gamela of Viana
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid game1240 'Gamela of Viana' (page and JSON record).
sources.note: No descriptive references; lists only Nimuendajú 1937 and Ribeiro 1841, both typed 'a wordlist or less'.

sources.citation: Jolkesky, Marcelo Pinho de Valhery. 2016. Estudo arqueo-ecolinguístico das terras tropicais sul-americanas. Doctoral dissertation, Universidade de Brasília.
sources.note: Open comparative dissertation that may cite the Gamela wordlist; repositorio.unb. Comparative only; no stress statement expected.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. pp. 91-92 (Gamela stock).
sources.note: Nothing. 'Gamela or Acobu or Barbados - extinct language once spoken on the Itapucurú, Turiaçú, and Pindaré Rivers.. [Nimuendajú 1937a, p. 68.]'; reproduces three words (kokeáto pot, kyoipé tree, anéno tobacco) in the comparative table. Secondary to Nimuendajú.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1937. The Gamella Indians (trans. Robert H. Lowie). Primitive Man 10(3/4): 58-71. DOI 10.2307/3316456.
sources.note: Nothing. The only linguistic content is a 19-word list on p. 68 ('this yielded only 19 vocables, viz.: tatá fire, purú, sebú, katú-brohó Negro, katú-koyaká White? Indian?, múisi brother-in-law, kokeáto pot, kutubé gourd bowl, tamarána club, kasapó knife, yopopó jaguar, kokói monkey, pohoné horse, azutí cattle, kurëká domestic fowl, kyoipé tree, anéno tobacco, birizu pepper, tomabéto thick'), followed by 'So far as this handful of words permits any conclusion, Gamella as spoken at Vianna must be treated as isolated.' Acute accents are written on 18 of the 19 items (12 final-syllable, 5-6 penul…

sources.citation: Ribeiro, Francisco de Paula. 1841 [written 1819]. Memoria sobre as nações gentias que presentemente habitam o Continente do Maranhão. Revista Trimensal do Instituto Historico e Geographico Brasileiro 3(10): 184-197; 3(11): 297-322; 3(12): 442-456.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnohistorical memoir; §23-24 'Dos gentios Gamellas de Vianna' and §31-35 'Dos gentios Gamellas do Codó' describe territory, warfare and weapons; the only Gamela-related word is the weapon name 'tamaranna'. Glottolog's second and last reference for game1240.
Nothing on phonology or stress; both rest entirely on Nimuendajú 1937 (cite also Loukotka 1968 and Kaufman 1994 for classification).

sources.citation: Kaufman, Terrence. 1994. The native languages of South America. In C. Mosley & R. E. Asher (eds.), Atlas of the world's languages, 46-76. London: Routledge.
